guide.it.code_couleur:
The colour of a noun shows its gender:

  • il, lo, l' in blue: masculine (il libro, lo zaino, l'amico)
  • la, l' in red: feminine (la casa, l'amica)
  • No colour: verbs, adjectives, adverbs and expressions, which have no article

Before a vowel, lo and la become l': then only the colour tells you the gender. The plural is written in full, with its article: gli amici, le amiche, le città (unchanged).

Linking a colour to the gender helps visual memory, especially for nouns ending in -e (il fiore, la chiave) and for traps (la mano, il problema).
guide.de.code_couleur:
The colour of a noun shows its gender, as in German textbooks:

  • der in blue: masculine
  • die in red: feminine
  • das in green: neuter
  • No colour: verbs, adjectives, adverbs and expressions, which have no article

For verbs with a preposition, the case to use is shown after the preposition: warten auf (+ Akk.), abhängen von (+ Dat.).

Linking a colour to the gender helps visual memory: over time, you'll “see” die Spinne in red.
guide.it.quiz_articles:
In the EN → IT direction, for each noun, choose il, lo, l' or la before seeing the answer (i, gli or le for a noun used only in the plural). A wrong article caps your grade at “Hard”: you only know the word if you know its article too.

Reminder: lo before s + consonant, z, gn, ps, x, y (lo studente, lo zio); l' before a vowel; il elsewhere.
guide.de.quiz_articles: In the EN → DE direction, for each noun, choose der, die or das before seeing the answer. A wrong article caps your grade at “Hard”: you only know the word if you know its article too.
guide.it.coller_format: il cane, i cani ; the dog ; example
guide.it.lettres: • The à è é ì ò ù buttons under the fields insert these letters.
guide.de.lettres: • The ä ö ü ß buttons under the fields insert these letters. In the exercises, you can also type ae, oe, ue and ss: they are accepted.

In Add, type an Italian word (or its English translation): the app finds the word in Memolex's lists, with its article, plural and reviewed translation. Tap a result to fill in the form. Everything works offline, without AI.

The Italian dictionary contains the 8,000 words of the lists. For a missing word, fill in the form yourself: article, plural with its article (gli zaini), translation.
guide.de.dictionnaire:
In Add, type a German word (or its English translation): the app finds the word in Memolex's lists, with its article, plural and reviewed translation. Tap a result to fill in the form. Everything works offline, without AI.

Estimated level (≈ A1-A2, ≈ B1-B2, ≈ C1+): calculated from how often the word is used in writing and speech. Very frequent words are usually learned early, rare words later. It is an approximation, not the official CEFR ranking: Kühlschrank is a beginner's word, but it is not frequent in texts. In My words, these levels have their own filter, separate from the exact levels.

For now, the German-English dictionary contains the words of the lists already translated into English. For a missing word, fill in the form yourself: article, plural, translation. If you type in English, reverse search works from 3 letters.

Sources: genders and plurals from the German-French dictionary FreeDict / WikDict (2022 edition) and the german-nouns project, both drawn from Wiktionary; results ranked by frequency of use thanks to wordfreq. Licences CC BY-SA 3.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0. English translations written for Memolex.

renderGuide.une_fois_installee_memolex_s: Once installed, Memolex opens like an app and works offline. The dictionary downloads the first time you open it.
renderGuide.l_appli_utilise_la_repetitio: The app uses spaced repetition: each word comes back just before you forget it. A well-known word is spaced out more and more (1 day, 3 days, a week, a month…). A missed word comes back quickly. So you spend your time on what resists, not on what you already know.
renderGuide.la_cle_chercher_activement_l: The key: actively search for the word before turning the card over. It's the effort of recall that fixes the memory, not rereading.
renderGuide.avant_chaque_session_choisis: Before each session, choose 20, 40 or 60 cards. Allow about 10 seconds per card. You can do as many sessions in a row as you like.
renderGuide.contenu_d_une_session_d: What's in a session: first the words to review (learning, then today's reviews), then new words to fill it up. If there are 15 words to review and you choose 40 cards, you'll get 15 reviews and 25 new words.
renderGuide.un_nouveau_mot_passe_3: A new word comes up 3 times: when you first see it, about 15 minutes later, then about 3 hours later. After that it is scheduled in days (tomorrow, then 3 days, a week…).
renderGuide.pas_de_limite_de_nouveaux: No limit on new words: you set the pace. Each new word comes back about 5 times in the first month, so lots of new words today means lots of reviews in the coming days.
renderGuide.une_session_longue_d_un: One long session in one go sticks less well than several short ones: 20 cards in the morning, 20 at lunchtime and 20 in the evening are better than 60 in a row.
renderGuide.reviser_quand_meme_quand_il: Review anyway: when there's nothing to review, free practice lets you go over your words without waiting. Your answers aren't saved there and don't change your schedule.
renderGuide.arreter_chaque_reponse_est_e: Stop: each answer is saved as soon as you give your grade. You can stop a session at any time without losing anything. If the app closes in the middle of a session (call, battery, phone put down), it offers to resume where you left off when you come back, even hours later. “Stop” ends the session for good.
renderGuide.revenir_en_arriere_la_fleche: Go back: the ‹ arrow to the left of the card takes you back to cards already seen, with the answer shown and your grade highlighted. Choose another grade to correct it, or move forward with the › arrow to the current card. There's no › arrow on a card you haven't answered yet: you can't skip a card.
renderGuide.les_listes_commencent_par_le: The lists start with the most frequent words, which you may already know. Two ways to set them aside:
renderGuide.je_connais_deja_sous_un: I already know it, under a new word during the session, once the answer is shown: you first check that you really knew it.
renderGuide.trier_mes_nouveaux_mots_avan: Sort my new words, before the session: each word appears with its translation, and you answer “I already know it” or “To learn”. 100 words take 2 or 3 minutes to sort.
renderGuide.un_mot_ecarte_n_est: A word set aside isn't deleted: it comes back once in a month to check. If you know it, it's spaced out further. To remove it for good, delete it in My words.
renderGuide.dans_l_onglet_stats_activer: In the Stats tab, “Turn on notifications” asks your phone for permission. You need to be signed in to sync: the server sends the notifications, even when the app is closed.
renderGuide.les_rappels_matin_midi_soir: Reminders (morning, lunchtime, evening, as you choose) only arrive if you haven't done your daily minimum of cards yet. The word of the day is a word from A1 to C2 that you don't have yet; the notification's “Add” button puts it in your words, first among the new ones.
renderGuide.sur_iphone_les_notifications: On iPhone, notifications only work if the app is added to the home screen.
renderGuide.une_journee_compte_dans_ta: A day counts towards your streak when you answer at least 10 cards in a session (adjustable: 5, 10, 20 or 30). Free practice doesn't count.
renderGuide.l_objectif_est_de_5: The goal is 5 days out of 7 by default: each week (Monday to Sunday) therefore gives you 2 jokers. The streak only breaks if you miss more days than you have jokers in the same week. You can change the goal or turn off the streak in the Stats tab.
renderGuide.l_onglet_stats_montre_les: The Stats tab shows words learned by level, reviews over the next 7 days, your success rate on mature words (interval of 21 days or more), your active days this month and your error rate on article and case. Only your first answer to each card in a session counts. You choose which statistics are shown.
renderGuide.une_traduction_te_parait_fau: Does a translation look wrong, or an example sentence odd or shocking? Once the answer is shown, tap ⚑ Report an error at the bottom of the card, choose the reason and add a comment if you like. The report includes the card as you see it. It's sent even without an account; offline, it waits for the next connection. Each reported error is corrected in the lists for all words of the same kind, not just for this card.
renderGuide.touche_a_cote_d_un: Tap 🔊 next to a word, a “Remember” phrase or an example sentence to hear it. A noun is read with its article (“{0}”): hearing the article with the word helps you remember the gender. It's your phone's synthetic voice: fine for common words, sometimes approximate on rare or very long words.
renderGuide.dans_le_sens_langue_francais: In the language → English direction, the word can be read on the front: good listening practice. In the English → language direction, it's only read on the back, so as not to give away the answer. Stats tab, Settings: Autoplay (the word is read as soon as it appears), normal or slow Speed, or turn pronunciation off.
renderGuide.pour_progresser_vraiment_rep: To really make progress, repeat the word out loud right after the voice, with the same intonation: this is the shadowing technique. If no voice speaks, install the language in your phone's text-to-speech settings (Android: Accessibility → Text-to-speech).
renderGuide.chaque_geste_a_son_petit: Each action has its little sound: the card turning over, a rising note for “Good” and “Easy”, a lower note for “Again” and “Hard”, a signal when the article or case is wrong, a chord at the end of the session. They stay discreet and follow the phone's volume (nothing in silent mode on iPhone). To turn them off: Stats tab, Settings, “Sounds”.
renderGuide.tu_ne_savais_pas_son: You didn't know it. Its interval starts again from zero and the card comes back at the end of the session: once all the other cards are done, the app announces the reinforcement and goes back over your “Again” cards. Each word comes back at most 3 times in a session: beyond that, repeating doesn't help much, spacing is better. The word waits for you in your next session.
renderGuide.trouve_avec_peine_l_interval: Found with difficulty. The interval grows a little.
renderGuide.trouve_normalement_la_note_p: Found normally. The default grade, the one used most.
renderGuide.immediat_l_intervalle_s_allo: Instant. The interval grows a lot.
renderGuide.sois_honnete_noter_bien_un: Be honest: grading “Good” a word you hesitated over means it comes back too late.
renderGuide.listes_par_niveau_les_8: Lists by level: the 8,000 most frequent words, from A1 to C2, added 50 at a time. The first A1 words are the most used in the language.
renderGuide.coller_une_liste_une_ligne: Paste a list: one line per word, {0}.
renderGuide.garde_fou_au_dela_de: Safeguard: beyond 50 words in progress (new, learning or in review), bulk additions (level packs, lessons, pasted list) stop. A word frees its place when it becomes “Learned” (3-week interval) or when you sort it as “I already know it”. Adding one word at a time (form, dictionary, word of the day) is always possible.
renderGuide.pour_annuler_un_import_mes: To undo an import: My words → Remove a batch. Words already started are kept.
renderGuide.quand_tu_retournes_une_carte: When you turn a card over, a word from the lists comes with a real sentence in {0}, with its translation. The word is underlined, in the form it takes in the sentence: {1}
renderGuide.une_phrase_par_sens_si: One sentence per sense: if a word has several translations, each has its own sentence, with the sense shown above it ({0}).
renderGuide.les_phrases_sont_choisies_co: Sentences are chosen to be short, with words that are rather more frequent than the word being learned, and preferably written by native speakers.
renderGuide.lis_la_phrase_a_voix: Read the sentence out loud before grading the card: a few more seconds, but the word sticks with its grammar.
renderGuide.si_tu_as_ecrit_ton: If you wrote your own example for a word, that's the one shown.
renderGuide.quand_plusieurs_de_tes_mots: When several of your words have the same translation ({0}), the card gives you a hint: the first letter and the number of letters of the expected word. On the back, the other words with the same translation are shown, so you learn to tell them apart.
renderGuide.si_tu_as_trouve_un: If you found another word from the list, it isn't wrong: grade it “Hard” and look at the difference in usage in the example sentence.
renderGuide.les_phrases_d_exemple_et: The example sentences and their translations come from Tatoeba, a collection of sentences written by volunteers, and are distributed under the CC BY 2.0 FR licence.
renderGuide.quelques_phrases_qui_precise: A few sentences, which clarify the nuance between two words with the same translation, were written for Memolex; they have no Tatoeba number. When Tatoeba has no English translation of a sentence, the translation was written for Memolex.
renderGuide.les_expressions_a_retenir_un: The “Remember” phrases (one per card, on the back) are written for Memolex: they show the word's most common use, with its usual complements.
renderGuide.les_listes_suivent_la_freque: The lists follow frequency of use: a word that is very common in writing and speech comes early, a rare word later. It's the most efficient way to start, because the few hundred most frequent words cover most of what you read and hear every day.
renderGuide.ces_tranches_sont_une_approx: These bands are an approximation of the Common European Framework, not its official ranking. Useful words that are not frequent in writing ({0}) come later than in a textbook: add them yourself with the dictionary when you need them.
renderGuide.combien_de_nouveaux_mots_par: How many new words per day?
renderGuide.une_fois_le_rythme_installe: Once the pace is set (after 3 or 4 weeks), your daily review load is proportional to the number of words you discover each day:
renderGuide.estimations_pour_environ_10_: Estimates for about 10 seconds per card. The real time depends on your speed and success rate.
renderGuide.sur_un_niveau_facile_pour: On a level that's easy for you, sort your packs then move fast: known words disappear and you don't waste time. On a new level, start with 10 new words per day (the default setting, in Stats → Settings) and go up to 15 or 20 only if your sessions stay comfortable. The app never goes beyond that number in a day, even if you choose a 60-card session: the rest of the session is made of reviews. If your sessions fill up with reviews to the point of leaving no room for new words, it's the signal to slow down: a pace kept up for six months is better than a two-week sprint.
